sentences.text:
And  In Re: Saddabur Seikh @ Sk.
 Petitioner  Mr. Manas Kumar Das  Mr. Aritra Kumar Thokdar  For the petitioner  Mr. Sujoy Sarkar  For the State  1.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on the date of incident he was not present and he has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
3. It is further submitted that the present petitioner is similarly circumstanced as that of the other accused persons, who have been granted anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State in opposing the prayer of anticipatory bail has referred to the statement of the victim, the injury report and the opinion of the Doctor.

5. Considering the materials available in the case diary and having regard to the statement of the victim and the injury report, we find sufficient incriminating materials as against the present accused petitioner.
